matches.gold_text: Proposals must be emailed to the Research Director at MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by 10 a.m. Central on the due date, August 21, 2024, according to the email time stamp.
The submittal must include a project plan, the proposed project team and its background, and any related projects now active or recently completed by the firm.
Questions and comments about the RFP must be sent to the Research Director by email by the deadline of 7/17/2024, 4 p.m. Central.
The proposal must include all data required in the Required Elements of Proposal section, or it may be disqualified.
The proposal should reference the project number and title, since more than one RFP may be due at the same time.
The Work Plan section of the proposal should be no longer than ten pages and use a font size of at least 12 points, excluding forms and resumes.
The project plan must include all items outlined in Section 2 (Scope of Work).
The project plan must recognize MoDOT's ultimate authority to approve the work plans.
Proposals must include a work plan with a proposed timeline.
The Personnel section should give the name, location, telephone number and email address of the Offeror's primary contact person.
The Offeror must provide a complete listing of each sub-offeror, if any, with complete contact information.
The proposal must clearly identify the Offeror's experience in offering the requested services during the past three years.
Proposals should give the name, title and telephone number of at least three client officials from within the past three years as references.
The proposal must be submitted as a single combined PDF document.

The proposal must contain only the required documents, in this order: Proposal Submission Form, Cover Letter, Body of Proposal (including work plan and project schedule), Personnel, Organization's Project Experience, Team Member Experience, and Organization's Client References.
A cover letter is optional and, if included, must not exceed one page.
The Offeror must submit a proposed cost estimate covering all services defined in the Scope of Work.
The cost estimate must be shown on the Section (4) Price Page, which must be completed, signed and returned with the proposal.
The services must be provided for a price not exceeding $175,000.
The contract period will be 15 months.
The Offeror must submit quarterly updates on work accomplished on or before the last working day of March, June, September and December throughout the project.
The quarterly updates must be submitted electronically to the MoDOT project manager.
An interim presentation to update MoDOT on progress must be completed by 9/15/2025.
The Offeror must provide ongoing progress updates by email and phone to MoDOT contacts every month.
The draft final report, summary report and user manual are due 11/3/2025.
The final report, summary report, presentation and user manual are due 1/1/2026, about one month before the contract ends.
The final invoice is due and the contract ends on 2/2/2026.
The Offeror must facilitate a kick-off meeting with MoDOT to review the work plan, scope and schedule and to establish a protocol for regular communications and coordination.
The Offeror must schedule and conduct quarterly project status meetings reviewing past progress and upcoming work, in person or online.
The Offeror must develop minutes for the kick-off meeting and each quarterly status meeting.
The Offeror must submit a Data Management Plan to MoDOT within two weeks after the project kick-off meeting.
The Data Management Plan should address use of platform-independent, non-proprietary data formats to maximize future utility of the data.
The Offeror must conduct a thorough literature search and review of other state DOT practices using AI/ML for right-of-way purposes.
Before work begins on the proof of concept, the Offeror must provide the name of the program used to develop the legal land descriptions.
MoDOT Information Systems must approve the program before the Offeror proceeds to Task 3c (proof of concept).
The Offeror must demonstrate that the technology can create draft legal land descriptions on a variety of properties.
The Offeror must provide training to MoDOT right-of-way staff once the system is developed and finalized.
The training must come with a user manual for staff to reference.
The Offeror must prepare a draft Synthesis Report and Research Summary with all accompanying documentation identified as beneficial during the study.
The draft documents should be final products apart from revisions based on MoDOT's review.
The final report must include a completed Technical Report Documentation page.
The Offeror must develop a final report detailing the tasks completed and all findings from the project.
The Offeror must provide a 1-2 page research summary stating the project objectives, findings and conclusions.
The Offeror must provide a presentation for MoDOT staff summarizing important details of the project.
Property descriptions prepared for MHTC must meet the requirements of the MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide.
Property rights acquired or conveyed by MHTC must be described using the metes and bounds method unless the property is acquired in its entirety.
When a property is acquired in its entirety, the description must be written exactly as it appears on the last deed of record.
Offerors are encouraged to obtain 10% MBE and 5% WBE participation.
All documents and reports produced by the Offeror at MHTC's direction, and information supplied by MHTC, remain MHTC's property.
MHTC may reproduce and use any products derived from the Offeror's work without paying royalties or fees.
The Offeror should be able to provide certificates of general liability insurance of at least $500,000 per person per occurrence and $3,000,000 per occurrence overall.
The Offeror should be able to provide certificates of automobile liability insurance of at least $500,000 per person per occurrence and $3,000,000 per occurrence overall.
The Offeror should be able to provide a Missouri workers' compensation policy or equivalent as required by state law.
All applications must be developed with an approved runtime: a currently supported .NET 6.0 or later release, or .NET Framework 4.8 or later only where specifically needed.
Web applications must use the MVC, Razor Pages or Web API framework.
Vendors may not use third-party tools or software that place a licensing responsibility on MoDOT without prior approval from the IS Best Practices Review Team and IS management.
Large-scale use of Python requires approval of the IS Best Practices Review Team.
Customer applications should be web-based, browser applications.
Applications should be tested and designed for the latest IS-approved browsers at a minimum.
No client-side software other than a modern browser should be required to run the web application.
On-premise database deployments must run on Oracle 19C or on the latest supported SQL Server (SQL Server 2016 or higher only if approved by MoDOT IS).
No personally identifiable information may be stored in any database table unless the application has a specific business need for it.
Any stored PII must be approved by the IS Cyber Security Team.
All web applications must conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA.
Content from another author's web pages must not be used unless the author explicitly allows free copying or arrangements are made with the author.
The Offeror must present how the AI/ML will create draft legal land descriptions by 4/25/2025.

New development should use the approved programming languages: C#, JavaScript, CSS and HTML (Python only for limited uses).
All web applications must meet the State of Missouri Accessibility Standard, based on Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act and the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines.
Vendor logos, branding or endorsements must not appear in the application where a supported, licensed option exists to remove them.
Library dependencies used in the application should be reviewed and updated annually.

verdicts.text: The proposal must be submitted to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by August 21, 2024 at 10 a.m. Central.

checklist.fact: The RFP is issued by the Missouri Highways and Transportation Commission (MHTC), coordinated by the Research Unit of the Construction and Materials Division, for MoDOT as the beneficiary (Right of Way staff are the users of the tool).
The need: property descriptions for MHTC must be written by metes and bounds and reviewed by a professional land surveyor, and these descriptions are long and tedious to write.
The project goal is to determine the usefulness of AI and ML to develop a "first draft" legal land description using MHTC parameters, which MoDOT Right of Way staff would review and edit.
The services are capped at a not-to-exceed price of $175,000.
The contract period is 15 months, with the project assumed to start November 1, 2024 and the contract ending February 2, 2026 with the final invoice due.
Proposals for project TR202504 must be emailed to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by August 21, 2024 at 10 a.m. Central.
Questions must be submitted by 7/17/2024 4 p.m. Central via the RFP email only; contacting MoDOT employees by other methods is prohibited and is cause for disqualification.
Property descriptions must meet the requirements of MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide (EPG) Section 236.4.6.2, which the RFP references but does not include.

Core deliverables include a data management plan, a proof-of-concept demonstration of AI writing legal land descriptions, training and a user manual for ROW staff, and draft and final reports; the final report, summary, presentation and user manual are due 1/1/2026.
The Offeror must name the program used to develop the LLDs before proof-of-concept work, and MoDOT Information Systems must approve it before Task 3c proceeds.
Web applications must meet WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility conformance.
No PII may be stored in any database table unless there is a specific business need, and any stored PII requires approval from the IS Cyber Security Team.

specificity.reason: Components name concrete deliverables, dates, roles, phases and conventions, though the AI/ML model approach, tooling and literature review sources stay fairly high-level.

feasibility.reason: Plausible within $175k, but a small team must build a model, web app and Oracle-backed system; the training data is thin, and the schedule leaves no room for IS approval delays.

consistency.reason: Mostly honors the technology, licensing and pricing constraints, but the plan puts a web app on Oracle and says nothing about PII or Python use for AI/ML. It also contradicts itself on the milestone dates.

component_records.title: Project management, governance and MoDOT coordination
component_records.description: A named project manager runs the study against a work plan that details every task, resource and schedule commitment and explicitly recognises MoDOT's ultimate authority to approve work plans (R046, R079). A kick-off meeting with MoDOT reviews work plan, scope and schedule and establishes the protocol for regular ongoing communications and coordination (R043); quarterly status meetings review the previous period's progress and the next period's anticipated work (R044), and written minutes are produced for the kick-off and every quarterly status meeting (R045). Meeting agendas and minutes are issued as task deliverables alongside the Data Management Plan (R022). Quarterly written updates are submitted on or before the last working day of March, June, September and December for the duration of the project (R028), and monthly e-mail and telephone updates keep MoDOT contacts informed between quarters (R031). An interim presentation is scheduled at the project mid-point to update MoDOT on progress and direction (R030). The team fully coordinates its activities with the Construction and Materials Division (R100) and keeps advice and information on matters covered by the Agreement available to that Division throughout the Agreement (R101), consulting MHTC's representative on any concern about administration of the services (R064). All work is planned inside the 15-month contract period (R015) and the schedule is built so the final invoice is raised and the contract closed on 2/2/2026 (R040). Every meeting, presentation, demonstration and submission the team schedules — kick-off, quarterly status meetings, the interim presentation, the 4/25/2025 demonstration, training and report deliveries — is booked inside the 7:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. Central window, and the project calendar carries that window as a standing constraint so no RFP event falls outside it (R016).

component_records.title: Literature review of state DOT AI/ML right-of-way practice
component_records.description: A structured literature search and review of other state DOT practices using AI/ML for right-of-way purposes (R050), covering published research, DOT reports and peer-state programme documentation, with a documented search protocol, inclusion criteria and a synthesis of transferable practice that feeds the proof-of-concept design. The review is delivered as a written chapter of the draft and final reports so MoDOT can see the evidence base behind the chosen approach.

component_records.title: Data Management Plan and data handling
component_records.description: A Data Management Plan is submitted to MoDOT within two weeks of the kick-off meeting (R047). It describes the anticipated formats of the study's data and related files (R048) and commits to platform-independent, non-proprietary formats so the data retains maximum future utility for MoDOT (R049). The plan also records how MoDOT-supplied example legal land descriptions are stored, versioned and separated from any live production data.

component_records.title: Program approval gate with MoDOT Information Systems
component_records.description: Before any proof-of-concept work begins, the team names the program used to develop the LLDs and submits it for approval by MoDOT Information Systems, and no Task 3c activity starts until that approval is received (R052). The submission pack documents the runtime, frameworks, languages and any libraries against the RFP's approved technologies so the Information Systems Best Practices Review Team can assess it in one pass (R132). The design uses a currently supported .NET 6.0 or above release, falling back to a supported .NET Framework 4.8+ only where a specific need is demonstrated (R133, R134), and web applications are built on MVC, Razor Pages or Web API (R135). Development uses the approved languages C#, JavaScript, CSS, HTML and Python (R138), with Python 3.x from python.org confined to ESRI scripts and small one-time uses unless the Best Practices Review Team approves larger-scale use (R139, R140). Library dependencies are reviewed and updated annually (R136).

component_records.title: AI/ML legal land description drafting engine
component_records.description: The core build: a model and rule set trained on MoDOT's previously approved and filed descriptions that generates a first draft of the legal land description from MHTC parameters, ready for Right of Way staff to review and edit (R014). The engine enforces the drafting conventions the RFP requires: metes and bounds descriptions for partial acquisitions (R012), verbatim reproduction of the last deed of record where a property is acquired in its entirety (R013), and output structured to satisfy MoDOT EPG Section 236.4.6.2, including recital of specific rights where less than fee simple title is conveyed (R011). The study is delivered as the TR202504 research programme for MHTC and MoDOT, with the drafting engine as its principal technical output (R010).

component_records.title: Browser-based application on MoDOT-approved platform
component_records.description: The drafting tool is delivered as a web-based browser application requiring no client-side software beyond a modern browser, with no Java Applets and no Silverlight (R141, R144), tested against the latest IS-approved browsers (R142). It runs on Oracle 19C for on-premise deployment (R145), with SQL Server 2016 or higher only where the MoDOT IS Data Service Management team approves it (R146). The interface meets WCAG 2.1 AA and the State of Missouri Accessibility Standard (R150). No Personal Identifiable Information is stored in any database table without a specific business need (R147) and any PII that is stored is approved by the IS Cyber Security Team (R148). No third-party tool or software is used that would place a licensing responsibility on MoDOT without prior review and approval by the Best Practices Review Team and IS management (R137), and vendor logos or branding are suppressed wherever a supported, licensed option exists to remove them (R152). All text, diagrams, images, source code and graphics are original or used with the author's explicit permission or an appropriate arrangement (R151).

component_records.title: Proof of concept and demonstration on MoDOT properties
component_records.description: A proof of concept in which the team demonstrates, on a variety of MoDOT-supplied properties, how the technology creates draft legal land descriptions (R053). The demonstration is presented to MoDOT on 4/25/2025, showing how the AI/ML produces draft LLDs, after which MoDOT's feedback is captured and fed into a documented refinement cycle (R035). Each draft is reviewed by the project's professional land surveyor before it is shown, so the demonstration reflects the review-and-edit workflow ROW staff will actually use.

component_records.title: Training, user manual and change management for ROW staff
component_records.description: Once the system is developed and finalised, the team trains Right of Way staff on its use (R054) and supplies a user manual for staff to reference (R055). Training is delivered as hands-on sessions built around the review-and-edit workflow, with the manual covering the drafting conventions, the metes-and-bounds and entire-acquisition paths, and the surveyor review step; the manual is delivered in editable electronic form so MoDOT can maintain it after the contract ends.

component_records.title: Research reporting: draft and final reports, summaries and presentation
component_records.description: A draft Synthesis Report and Research Summary are prepared together with all accompanying documentation identified as beneficial during the study (R056), and are delivered as final products except for revisions arising from MoDOT's review (R057). A draft report, summary and user manual are submitted as a package (R025), and the final report, summary, presentation and user manual are delivered at close-out (R026). The final report details every task completed and all findings generated during the project (R060); a 1-2 page research summary states the objectives, findings and conclusions (R061); and a presentation for MoDOT staff summarises the significant details of the project (R062).

component_records.title: Contract, compliance, insurance and pricing obligations
component_records.description: A compliance workstream owns every contractual and legal obligation in the RFP. The bid is offered at the fees quoted under the terms of the RFP (R007) and the services are provided for a total not to exceed $175,000 (R041), with a cost estimate covering all Scope of Work services (R092) broken out into Salaries, Benefits, Operating Expense, Facilities and Administration (F&A) and Miscellaneous with a Total (R096), and miscellaneous costs itemised on an additional sheet where needed (R097). The awarded contract incorporates the contract provisions specified in the RFP (R098), and the Offeror accepts that MHTC may cancel the award and select another Offeror if post-award terms cannot be agreed (R099). The Agreement is accepted as comprising the RFP and its written amendments, the proposal and the signed post-award contract (R105), with MHTC's written clarifications governing over conflicts (R106) and any change made only by formal signed amendment (R107). The Offeror remains ultimately responsible and liable to MHTC for the complete, accurate and professional quality and performance of the services regardless of subcontractors or suppliers (R112), and will not assign, delegate or novate any interest without MHTC's prior written consent (R103). items.text: The RFP is issued by the Missouri Highways and Transportation Commission (MHTC) on behalf of the Missouri Department of Transportation (MoDOT), with the study coordinated by the Research Unit of the Construction and Materials Division.

MoDOT's Right of Way staff currently prepare and review legal land descriptions for realty rights MHTC acquires or conveys, and every description must be reviewed by a professional land surveyor before a general warranty deed, quitclaim deed or similar document is presented to the grantor.

Descriptions must use the metes and bounds method unless the property is acquired in its entirety, in which case the description must be written exactly as it appears on the last deed of record, and must meet MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide (EPG) Section 236.4.6.2, reciting specific rights if less than fee simple title.
Writing these legal land descriptions is described in the RFP as long and tedious work, which is the pain point driving the study.
MoDOT already holds a body of previously approved and filed legal land descriptions that it will hand to the contractor as training material for the machine.

MoDOT's Information Systems group already governs the technology stack and must approve the program used before proof-of-concept work can proceed, so the client has an established IT review gate in place.
The RFP is open to private consultants, universities and research organizations, and MoDOT states it is seeking proposer input to determine the best strategies to accomplish the research objectives.

MoDOT wants a research study, TR202504 "Using AI/ML to Write Legal Land Descriptions," to determine the usefulness of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in producing a "first draft" legal land description from MHTC parameters that Right of Way staff can then review and edit.

The work is organized into six tasks: project management, a literature review of other state DOT practices using AI/ML for right-of-way purposes, a proof of concept (including MoDOT-supplied example LLDs and a demonstration of AI writing a description), training and a user manual, a draft report and research summary, and a final report, summary and presentation.
The contract period is 15 months, with the project schedule estimated to start November 1, 2024 and the contract ending 2/2/2026 when the final invoice is due.
The Offeror must demonstrate on a variety of properties how the technology creates draft legal land descriptions, with MoDOT reviewing the drafts and providing feedback for improvement.
Once the system is developed and finalized, the Offeror must train Right of Way staff and supply a user manual for them to reference.
The Offeror must deliver a final report detailing all tasks and findings, a 1-2 page research summary stating objectives, findings and conclusions, and a presentation for MoDOT staff.
The Offeror must conduct a thorough literature search and review of other state DOT practices using AI/ML for right-of-way purposes.

Proposals are due to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by August 21, 2024 at 10 a.m. Central, and a proposal is not considered submitted until the Offeror receives notification of receipt, which should arrive by noon the same day.

All questions and comments must go only to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by 7/17/2024 at 4 p.m. Central; contacting MoDOT employees by other methods is prohibited and is cause for disqualification, and MoDOT posts its responses publicly on 7/31/2024.
MoDOT notifies submitters on 9/18/2024 whether their proposal was selected or whether they are invited to interviews to finalize selection.

Award goes to the Offeror providing the best proposal, with proposals first checked for responsiveness and then evaluated against criteria established by the Technical Advisory Committee, whose specific criteria and weights are not listed in the RFP.

The Work Plan is limited to ten (10) pages with font no smaller than 12 points, excluding attached forms and resumes, and must cover all items in Section 2 while recognizing MoDOT's ultimate authority to approve work plans.

Proposals must be one combined PDF ordered as: Proposal Submission Form; optional one-page cover letter; body of proposal including work plan and project schedule; personnel; organization's project experience; team member experience; and organization's client references.

The proposal must identify experience delivering the requested services during the past three years and give the name, title and telephone number of at least three client officials from the past three years.

The Offeror must present how the AI/ML will create draft LLDs on 4/25/2025 for MoDOT feedback, deliver the manual and ROW staff training on 7/25/2025, complete the interim presentation by 9/15/2025, and submit the draft final report, summary and user manual by 11/3/2025.

Services are capped at a total not-to-exceed amount of $175,000, with costs itemized on the Section (4) Price Page across salaries, benefits, operating expense, facilities and administration (F&A), and miscellaneous.
Before proof-of-concept work begins, the Offeror must name the program used to develop the LLDs and obtain approval from MoDOT Information Systems.

Applications must be built on approved technologies: .NET 6.0 or above (or a supported .NET Framework 4.8+ where specifically needed), web applications using MVC, Razor Pages or Web API, with C#, JavaScript, CSS, HTML and Python as approved languages, Python reserved for ESRI scripts and small one-time uses unless large-scale use is approved by the Information Systems Best Practices Review Team.

No third-party tool or software may be used that would place a licensing responsibility on MoDOT without prior review and approval by the Information Systems Best Practices Review Team and IS management.

Applications must be browser-based with no client-side software beyond a modern browser (no Java Applets, no Silverlight), run on Oracle 19C or a supported SQL Server version (2016 or higher if approved by the MoDOT IS Data Service Management team), and meet WCAG 2.1 AA and the State of Missouri Accessibility Standard.
No Personal Identifiable Information may be stored in any database table without a specific business need and approval from the IS Cyber Security Team.

All documents, reports and exhibits the Offeror produces at MHTC's direction, and information supplied by MHTC, remain the property of MHTC, and MHTC may reproduce and use derived products without royalties or fees.

The Data Management Plan is due within 2 weeks after the kick-off meeting and must describe anticipated data and file formats and how platform-independent, non-proprietary formats will be used for maximum future utility.
The contract period is 15 months, with an estimated start of November 1, 2024 and the final invoice due 2/2/2026.
The study is coordinated by the Research Unit of MoDOT's Construction and Materials Division.
MoDOT will supply previously approved and filed legal land descriptions as training material for the machine.
MoDOT's Information Systems group governs the technology stack and must approve the program before proof-of-concept work can proceed.
Every legal land description must be reviewed by a professional land surveyor before a deed is presented to the grantor.
MoDOT holds a body of previously approved and filed legal land descriptions that it will hand over as training material.
The Offeror must demonstrate on a variety of properties how the technology creates draft legal land descriptions, with MoDOT reviewing drafts and providing feedback.
Services are capped at a total not-to-exceed amount of $175,000, itemised on the Section (4) Price Page.
All documents and reports produced at MHTC's direction, and information supplied by MHTC, remain MHTC property.

The MHTC parameters that drive the draft description are assumed to be the acquisition/conveyance inputs MoDOT Right of Way staff already assemble (parcel intent, deed of record, area to be taken, rights conveyed), supplied in a structured template agreed at kick-off.

MoDOT EPG Section 236.4.6.2 is assumed to be obtainable from MoDOT's published Engineering Policy Guide and to be the controlling drafting standard, so the drafting rules are encoded from that published section rather than from a bespoke specification.

The 11/15/2024 kick-off and the milestone dates in the RFP schedule (4/25/2025 demonstration, 7/25/2025 training and manual, 9/15/2025 interim presentation, 11/3/2025 draft deliverables, 1/1/2026 final documents, 2/2/2026 contract end) are treated as binding, with the November 1, 2024 start governing the proposed timeline.
The mid-point interim presentation is assumed to fall at month seven of the 15-month period, around May 2025, and is priced as one in-person or virtual session for MoDOT staff.

Training is assumed to be a small number of hands-on sessions for the Right of Way staff who will use the tool, delivered remotely with one on-site option, plus an editable electronic user manual; the exact headcount and session count are confirmed at kick-off.

The proof of concept is assumed to cover a representative sample of property types (partial takes by metes and bounds, entire acquisitions by deed of record, and less-than-fee interests) rather than an exhaustive parcel set, with the sample agreed with MoDOT before the 4/25/2025 demonstration.
The $175,000 not-to-exceed cap is assumed to be inclusive of all six tasks, travel, overhead and F&A, with no separate reimbursement.
The cost estimate is assumed to cover the full 15-month period of performance, not an annualised figure.
Oracle 19C is assumed to be the mandatory on-premise database platform, with SQL Server 2016+ used only if the MoDOT IS Data Service Management team approves it.

The approved technologies list is assumed to permit standard AI/ML libraries and frameworks within the approved languages, subject to the Best Practices Review Team's review of any licensing responsibility, and the named program is submitted for Information Systems approval at mobilisation so the gate does not delay the proof of concept.

The literature review is assumed to cover published state DOT research and peer-state programme documentation from the last decade across right-of-way use cases, delivered as a report chapter, since the RFP sets no narrower scope.

The Publication Guidelines and summary template are assumed to be the versions currently posted on MoDOT's website, and compliance with them is treated as a pass/fail formatting requirement for the final report and research summary.
The insurance limits are assumed to be binding contract requirements rather than indicative, and certificates meeting the stated amounts are held ready before contract signing.

The contract provisions referenced in the RFP are assumed to be the Standard Research Agreement published on MoDOT's website, accepted without negotiation of substance, with any conflict resolved in favour of MHTC's written clarifications.
The 10% MBE / 5% WBE participation is assumed to be measured against total contract value and is pursued as a target through subcontracting, with attainment reported in the proposal.

The 7/17/2024 4 p.m. Central deadline is assumed to be the cutoff for questions and comments, and the 7:30 a.m.-4 p.m. window is assumed to constrain MoDOT's own actions rather than the bidder's electronic submission.

Information Systems approval gate can stall the proof of concept. No Task 3c work may start until MoDOT Information Systems approves the named program, and the RFP sets no approval criteria or turnaround time. The solution assumes approval is sought at mobilisation so the 4/25/2025 demonstration is not delayed, but if the review takes weeks or rejects the chosen AI/ML stack, the demonstration date and the whole 15-month schedule slip while the fixed price stands. The gate is a hard stop before the core technical work and the 4/25/2025 demonstration is a fixed milestone; the RFP gives no criteria or service level for the review, so the risk turns on facts it does not settle.

AI/ML libraries may not be on the approved technology list. The RFP requires development on an approved technologies list that is not reproduced, and reserves Python for ESRI scripts and small one-time uses unless the Best Practices Review Team approves larger-scale use. The proposed solution assumes standard AI/ML libraries and frameworks are permitted, but a model-training workload in Python is plausibly large-scale use, and any third-party library that places a licensing responsibility on MoDOT needs prior approval. A rejection would force a redesign of the core engine after the bid is priced. The engine is the principal technical output and depends on libraries the RFP does not confirm as approved; the solution's assumption that they are permitted is untested and the approval path is undefined.

Fixed $175,000 cap against an open-ended scope. The services are capped at a total not-to-exceed $175,000 covering all six tasks, travel, overhead and F&A, while several deliverables are defined only by reference to text not in the RFP and one is open-ended ("all accompanying documentation identified as beneficial during the study"). The solution prices a five-person senior team for 15 months inside that cap. If the training, demonstration or documentation scope grows, the bidder absorbs the overrun. The cap is firm and inclusive while the scope is partly undefined and partly open-ended; a senior team over 15 months against $175,000 leaves little margin for rework or scope growth.

Training and demonstration scope undefined at a fixed price. The RFP does not state how many ROW staff are trained, whether training is on-site or remote, how many sessions, or how many properties the 4/25/2025 demonstration must cover. The solution assumes a small number of remote sessions with one on-site option and a representative sample of property types. If MoDOT expects on-site training for a large staff or an exhaustive parcel set, the effort and travel cost rise with no price relief. Both deliverables are mandatory and dated, and the RFP leaves their size entirely open; the solution's assumptions are inferences, so the expected outcome is a mismatch unless MoDOT confirms the numbers.

Oracle 19C vs SQL Server conflict unresolved. The RFP mandates Oracle 19C for on-premise deployments in one place and permits SQL Server 2016+ with IS approval in another. The proposed solution commits to Oracle 19C as the primary platform while also describing SQL Server as an approved fallback, so the design, licensing and DBA effort are not settled. If MoDOT's environment turns out to be SQL Server-based, the data layer and deployment work would be reworked inside a fixed $175,000 cap. The two requirements are directly incompatible and the RFP does not say which governs; the solution resolves it by assumption rather than by a written clarification, so the choice rests on facts the RFP does not settle.

EPG Section 236.4.6.2 not supplied, drafting rules inferred. The descriptions must meet MoDOT EPG Section 236.4.6.2, but that section is not in the RFP and the solution assumes it can be taken from MoDOT's published Engineering Policy Guide. If the published section is not the controlling standard, or if MoDOT applies internal drafting conventions beyond it, the rule set encoded in the engine is wrong and the demonstration drafts and the training manual would need rework. The standard is mandatory and central to the engine's output, and the solution relies on an inference about where the controlling text lives rather than a confirmed copy.

MHTC parameters for the draft are undefined. The engine must produce a first draft from "MHTC parameters", but the RFP does not define what those parameters are or where they are documented. The solution assumes they are the acquisition inputs ROW staff already assemble, supplied in a structured template agreed at kick-off. If the real inputs are unstructured, incomplete or vary by parcel type, the input design and the model's preprocessing change after the price is fixed. The parameter set is the engine's primary input and is left undefined; the solution's structured-template assumption is an inference that MoDOT has not confirmed.

Exhibits A and B referenced but not in the RFP. The Agreement requirements section refers to Exhibit A and Exhibit B, which are not included in the RFP document. Exhibit B is the sworn affidavit of lawful presence that sole proprietors and general partners must submit, and Exhibit A is referenced for the non-employment affidavit. A bidder that cannot see them risks submitting an incomplete proposal or missing a flow-down obligation in subcontracts. The exhibits carry mandatory submission and subcontract obligations, and their absence means the bidder cannot confirm what must be signed and returned with the proposal.

Two unreadable pages may hide requirements. Pages 19 and 20 of the RFP carry almost no extractable text and are dominated by images, so their content could not be read. If those pages hold deliverable tables, schedule dates or mandatory forms, the bid could miss a requirement or misprice a deliverable without anyone noticing until evaluation. The pages sit in the section that carries the deliverable and schedule tables, and the solution's milestone assumptions are drawn from adjacent text, so unread content there could change the schedule or scope.

Milestone dates conflict with the contract end date. The RFP fixes the 4/25/2025 demonstration, 7/25/2025 training and manual, 9/15/2025 interim presentation and 11/3/2025 draft deliverables, but also says the later dates are to be determined at the 11/15/2024 kick-off and that final documents are due about a month before a contract that ends 2/2/2026. The solution treats all dates as binding and prices the interim presentation at month seven. If MoDOT moves the dates or the start slips past 1 November 2024, the schedule compresses against a fixed price. The RFP gives both fixed and to-be-determined dates and a start date that is only estimated; the solution resolves the conflict by assumption, so a slip or a re-dated milestone is plausible.

Accessibility conformance unverified for a data-heavy interface. The application must meet WCAG 2.1 AA and the State of Missouri Accessibility Standard, which is referenced only by link and not included. The drafting tool presents long legal text, tables of parcel data and generated descriptions, which are exactly the content types that fail AA conformance without deliberate design and testing. Remediation after the build would be unplanned work inside the cap. Conformance is mandatory and the referenced standard is not in the RFP, so the testing scope is not fully known; the interface's text- and table-heavy nature makes failures likely without an early audit.

Training material and code originality obligations. The RFP forbids using another author's text, diagrams, source code or graphics without explicit permission or an appropriate arrangement, and requires vendor branding to be suppressed where a licensed option exists. The solution plans to encode drafting rules from MoDOT's published EPG and to use open-source AI/ML libraries. If licence terms or EPG reproduction are not cleared, the deliverable could be rejected or require replacement late in the project. The obligation is mandatory but manageable with a licence review; the risk is real because the solution depends on third-party libraries and on reproducing published drafting standards.
